title: Checkpoint and resume long fits
text: Every nested-Laplace fitter takes control$checkpoint = list(path =, resume =). path checkpoint file; resume = TRUE reloads completed cells , resume = FALSE (default) starts fresh overwrites. grid cells now disk:
code: # A small nested-Laplace fit over an ICAR field on a chain graph. S <- 30L W <- matrix(0, S, S) for (i in 1:(S - 1)) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1 df <- data.frame(region = factor(seq_len(S))) df$x <- as.integer(df$region) / 10 + rnorm(S, 0, 0.3) df$y <- rbinom(S, 20, plogis(-0.4 + 0.5 * df$x))  ckpt <- tempfile(fileext = ".ckpt") fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = df, family = "binomial",              n_trials = rep(20L, S),              spatial = spatial_car(W, level = "obs"),              mode = "laplace",              control = list(checkpoint = list(path = ckpt, resume = FALSE))) coef(fit) file.exists(ckpt) && file.info(ckpt)$size > 0

code: GRID <- exp(seq(log(0.2), log(1.5), length.out = 7)) PHI  <- 0.7 BETA <- c(-0.2, 0.7)  simulate_one <- function(seed) {   set.seed(seed)   sigma  <- GRID[sample.int(length(GRID), 1L)]   region <- rep(seq_len(6L), each = 4L)   X      <- cbind(1, rnorm(24L))   u      <- rnorm(6L, 0, sigma)   list(y      = as.numeric(X %*% BETA) + u[region] + rnorm(24L, 0, PHI),        X      = X,        region = region,        theta  = c(beta1 = BETA[1], beta2 = BETA[2], sigma = sigma)) }  fit_one <- function(d, diagnose = FALSE) {   tulpa_nested_laplace(     y = d$y, n_trials = rep(1L, length(d$y)), X = d$X,     prior = list(list(type = "iid", obs_idx = d$region,                       n_units = max(d$region), sigma_grid = GRID)),     family = "gaussian", phi = PHI,     control = list(n_threads = 1L, keep_grid_hessians = TRUE,                    auto_recenter = FALSE, progress = FALSE,                    diagnose_k = diagnose, diagnose_skew = diagnose)) }

code: periodic_ar1 <- function(n) {   tgmrf(     Q = function(theta) {       sigma <- exp(theta[1]); rho <- tanh(theta[2])       d <- rep((1 + rho^2) / sigma^2, n)       o <- rep(-rho / sigma^2, n)       M <- Matrix::bandSparse(n, k = c(-1, 0, 1),                               diagonals = list(o, d, o))       M[1, n] <- M[n, 1] <- -rho / sigma^2     # wrap       methods::as(methods::as(M, "generalMatrix"), "CsparseMatrix")     },     prior = function(theta) {       dnorm(theta[1], 0, 1, log = TRUE) +     # weak on log_sigma       dnorm(theta[2], 0, 1, log = TRUE)       # weak on atanh_rho     },     init   = c(log_sigma = 0, atanh_rho = atanh(0.3)),     bounds = list(lower = c(log(0.3), atanh(0.0)),                   upper = c(log(3.0), atanh(0.9))),     name   = "periodic_ar1"   ) }

code: library(tulpa)  # Poisson counts with a correlated site-level intercept and slope set.seed(1) site <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 8) x    <- rnorm(320) b0   <- rnorm(40, 0, 0.7)                          # site intercepts (truth SD 0.7) b1   <- rnorm(40, 0, 0.4)                          # site slopes     (truth SD 0.4) y    <- rpois(320, exp(0.2 + (0.5 + b1[site]) * x + b0[site])) d    <- data.frame(y, x, site = factor(site))  fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x | site), data = d, family = "poisson")  fit$selection_reason #> "random-slope term(s) present; RE covariance(s) integrated via re_cov_gibbs (1 block(s))"  summary(fit) #>             estimate  std.error    2.5%   97.5% #> (Intercept)    0.214      0.103  -0.003   0.401 #> x              0.488      0.087   0.322   0.658  fit$posterior          # the random-effect covariance, marginalized to sigma / rho #>   parameter    mean     sd   median   ci_lo   ci_hi #>     sigma_1   0.688  0.102    0.678   0.516   0.918   # intercept SD (truth 0.7) #>     sigma_2   0.469  0.074    0.461   0.345   0.636   # slope SD     (truth 0.4) #>      rho_12  -0.145  0.206   -0.156  -0.523   0.254   # correlation  (truth 0)

Three routes share summary, selectable front door callable directly: tulpa_re_cov_gibbs() — exact debias via Metropolis-within-Gibbs conjugate inverse-Wishart draws (auto default slopes). tulpa_re_cov_nested() — nested-Laplace integration Sigma log-Cholesky coordinates (control = list(re_cov = "nested")). tulpa_re_aghq() — deterministic debias via adaptive Gauss–Hermite quadrature. what: Adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for one-RE GLMMs — agq_fit
title: Adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for one-RE GLMMs — agq_fit
text: Marginal-likelihood approximation generalised linear mixed model one cluster-level intercept random effect. Adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (AGQ) generalises Laplace replacing single-point Gaussian integral around cluster's posterior mode n_quad-point quadrature. AGQ n_quad = 1 recovers Laplace approximation; higher n_quad reduces approximation error, especially clusters observations non-Gaussian likelihoods. engine block, front door: tuning knobs (max_iter, tol, n_quad) sit signature rather control list. Fields: emits    – kind posterior representation backend's draws hold, fixes whether MCMC chain diagnostics apply (independent tier: exact SMC sampler emits "iid" particles, Tier-3 VI fit also emits "iid", nested-Laplace Tier-2 fit emits "iid" ): "chain" : autocorrelated MCMC output – Rhat autocorrelation-ESS meaningful (diagnostics() computes ). "iid"   : exchangeable draws deterministic approximation, resampled particles – split-Rhat vacuous ESS = n construction, say nothing approximation bias. CCD scales much better full tensor expand.grid() used 1D 2D backends: CCD \(1 + 2k + 2^{k - q}\) points (1 centre, 2k axial, \(2^{k - q}\) factorial), versus \(m^k\) m-per-axis tensor product. Point layout (centre+axial+factorial scaling \(f_0\)): 1 centre point origin; 2k axial points \(\pm f_0\) along coordinate axis; \(2^{k - q}\) factorial points corners hypercube, scaled lie sphere radius \(f_0\). \(k \le 6\) factorial portion full \(2^k\) design. \(k \ge 7\) half-fraction (\(q = 1\)) using defining word \(x_1 \cdots x_k\) keeps point count reasonable preserving Resolution V. Used tulpa_nested_laplace() higher-dimensional hyperparameter blocks. standardised z-coordinates mapped physical hyperparameters \(\theta\) via ccd_to_theta().

text: Per-point design weights ccd_grid() used nested-Laplace integration nodes. Implements corrected R-INLA central-composite-design weights: formula Rue, Martino Chopin (2009) typo, corrected R-INLA team give positive central weight. m hyperparameters, np design points standardized scaling f0, every non-centre point gets $$w = 1 / ((np - 1)(1 + e^{-m f0^2 / 2}(f0^2 - 1)))$$ centre point gets \(w_0 = 1 - (np - 1) w\). title: Fit a Spatial Model using SPDE Laplace Approximation — fit_spde
code: # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("fmesher", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   n <- 200L   coords <- cbind(runif(n), runif(n))   mesh <- fmesher::fm_mesh_2d(loc = coords, max.edge = c(0.15, 0.4), cutoff = 0.05)   fem  <- fmesher::fm_fem(mesh)   A    <- as(fmesher::fm_basis(mesh, loc = coords), "CsparseMatrix")   spec <- spatial_spde_custom(C = fem$c0, G = fem$g1, A = A, nu = 1,                               prior_range = c(0.3, 0.5), prior_sigma = c(0.6, 0.05))   w <- as.numeric(rnorm(spec$n_mesh, 0, 0.6)); w <- w - mean(w)   x <- rnorm(n)   y <- rpois(n, exp(2.0 + 0.5 * x + as.numeric(spec$A %*% w)))   fit <- fit_spde(y = y, X = cbind(1, x), spatial = spec, family = "poisson")   fit$nested$range_mean } #> [1] 0.07126109 # }

code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) n_s <- 16L; n_t <- 8L; N <- 400L adj <- matrix(0, n_s, n_s) for (i in 1:(n_s - 1)) adj[i, i + 1] <- adj[i + 1, i] <- 1 s <- sample(n_s, N, TRUE); tt <- sample(n_t, N, TRUE) us <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(n_s)))); vt <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(n_t)))) x <- rnorm(N) y <- rbinom(N, 1, plogis(0.2 + 0.5 * x + 0.7 * us[s] + 0.6 * vt[tt])) fit <- fit_st_nested(y, cbind(1, x), s, adj, tt, n_t, family = "binomial") # }

title: Independence Metropolis-Hastings with Laplace proposal — imh_laplace
code: # Toy: Bernoulli logistic with one covariate. set.seed(1) n <- 100 x <- rnorm(n) eta <- 0.3 + 1.2 * x y <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(eta)) X <- cbind(1, x)  lap <- tulpa_laplace(y, n_trials = rep(1L, n), X = X,                      family = "binomial")  log_post <- function(beta) {   eta <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)   sum(y * eta - log1p(exp(eta))) +     sum(dnorm(beta, 0, 10, log = TRUE)) }  fit <- imh_laplace(log_post, mode = lap$mode[1:2],                    hessian = lap$H_beta, n_iter = 1000) fit$mean_accept #> [1] 0.898 colMeans(fit$draws) #> [1] 0.4232243 1.2244703

title: Inference Mode System — inference_modes
text: Tier 1 - Exact: Asymptotically correct posterior inference (Monte Carlo error). Credible intervals interpretable posterior uncertainty. reference standard. Tier 2 - Structured: Accurate inference conditional explicit structural assumptions. Typically requires latent Gaussian structure, conditional independence, smooth posteriors. fast right model class, can wrong outside class. Failure modes predictable explainable. Tier 3 - Optimized: general correctness guarantee beyond empirical usefulness. Point estimates usually good, uncertainty often underestimated. Tails correlations unreliable. Failure usually silent. optimization, sampling.

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
text: modeling multiple processes, often share unmeasured confounders. example, relative abundance data, focal species count total count might affected : Observer skill (unmeasured) Local microhabitat conditions (unmeasured) Weather sampling day (unmeasured) Without accounting shared drivers, estimates can biased. Latent factors capture shared structure without requiring confounders measured.

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
text: observation K latent factors, two model arms (processes 1 2): $$\eta^{(1)}_i = X^{(1)}_i \beta^{(1)} + \sum_{k=1}^{K} f_{ik} \sigma_k + \ldots$$ $$\eta^{(2)}_i = X^{(2)}_i \beta^{(2)} + \sum_{k=1}^{K} f_{ik} \sigma_k + \ldots$$ : \(f_{ik} \sim N(0, 1)\) standardized factor scores \(\sigma_k\) factor standard deviations PC prior Identifiability: \(\sum_i f_{ik} = 0\) k factors enter linear predictors identically (shared), cancel derived quantities (e.g., ratios, differences): $$\eta^{(1)}_i - \eta^{(2)}_i$$ means factors capture shared effects otherwise bias derived quantities.

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
text: Start n_factors = 1 simple unmeasured confounding Use n_factors = 2-3 suspect multiple independent confounders 3 factors rarely needed risks overfitting PC prior provides regularization, shrinking unneeded factors toward zero

title: Create a latent factor specification — latent_factor
text: Latent factors differ random effects several ways: Random effects grouped (e.g., site-level), factors observation-level Random effects require grouping structure, factors Factors capture residual correlation explained observed predictors can use together: random effects known grouping, factors residual unmeasured confounding.

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: Sample posterior using MALA: Langevin proposal driven gradient log posterior, corrected Metropolis- Hastings accept/reject step. iteration one log-posterior + one gradient evaluation. natural stepping stone random-walk MH HMC: cheaper per iteration HMC (leapfrog integration), better-mixing RWMH drift term moves toward higher density. Step size epsilon adapted via dual averaging warmup target acceptance rate 0.574 (Roberts & Rosenthal 1998 optimal high-dimensional Gaussians).

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
code: mala(   log_posterior,   grad_log_posterior,   init,   n_iter = 2000L,   warmup = n_iter%/%2L,   epsilon = 0.1,   target_accept = 0.574,   mass_diag = NULL,   thin = 1L,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: log_posterior Function function(theta) -> numeric returning unnormalized log posterior. grad_log_posterior Function function(theta) -> numeric vector returning gradient theta. init Numeric vector: initial state (must give finite log_posterior). n_iter Total iterations including warmup (default 2000). warmup Warmup iterations (step-size adaptation + discarded; default n_iter / 2). epsilon Initial step size (default 0.1). Adapted warmup. target_accept Target acceptance warmup adaptation (default 0.574, Roberts & Rosenthal 1998 optimum). mass_diag Optional preconditioner: length-d vector per-dimension variances, used diagonal inverse-mass M^-1. proposal N(theta + (eps^2/2) * M^-1 * grad, eps^2 * M^-1), entry j scales proposal variance along dimension j noise standard deviation eps * sqrt(mass_diag[j]). Default rep(1, d). posteriors different scales across dimensions, set (estimate ) posterior variances, .e. squared posterior SDs. thin Keep every thin-th post-warmup sample (default 1). verbose Print acceptance + step-size summary end (default FALSE).

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: list class tulpa_fit carrying: draws: post-warmup draws. means, n_params, n_samples, log_prob. accept_prob: per-iteration accepted indicators (post-warmup). mean_accept: post-warmup acceptance rate. epsilon: final adapted step size. inference_mode: "exact". inference_tier: 1L. backend: "mala".

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: Tier 1 (Exact). MH step makes chain asymptotically correct. Mixing depends whether gradient gives useful local geometry – poor posteriors different scales across dimensions (use preconditioner HMC instead).

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: Roberts, G. O., & Tweedie, R. L. (1996). Exponential convergence Langevin distributions discrete approximations. Bernoulli, 2(4), 341-363. Roberts, G. O., & Rosenthal, J. S. (1998). Optimal scaling discrete approximations Langevin diffusions. JRSS B, 60(1), 255-268.

title: Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) — mala
code: log_post <- function(t) -0.5 * sum((t - c(1, 2))^2) grad <- function(t) -(t - c(1, 2)) fit <- mala(log_post, grad, init = c(0, 0), n_iter = 1000) colMeans(fit$draws)  # near c(1, 2) #> [1] 1.086552 2.030870 fit$mean_accept      # should adapt toward 0.574 #> [1] 0.604

title: Marginal fixed-effect Hessian for spatial-field Laplace fits — marginal_se_spatial
text: raw fixed-effect block joint Hessian gives conditional precision \(\beta \mid u^*\), -states uncertainty; returns marginal precision instead.

title: Marginal fixed-effect Hessian for spatial-field Laplace fits — marginal_se_spatial
text: correct marginal precision comes Schur complement joint Hessian mode: $$H_\beta^{\mathrm{marg}} = X'WX - X'WZ (Z'WZ + Q_u)^{-1} Z'WX$$ \(Z\) obs->latent map (SPDE: projection matrix ; NNGP: indicator obs unique-location field) \(Q_u\) spatial precision fitted hyperparameters. helpers rebuild spatial precision R spec fitted hyperparameters, solve via sparse Cholesky. shape matches cpp_laplace_fit_spde / cpp_laplace_fit_gp use internally – Q construction 1:1 port spde_qbuilder.h (orphan ridge included).

text: Single-path Pathfinder (Zhang, Carpenter, Gelman, Vehtari 2022): run L-BFGS toward posterior mode, fit Gaussian optimum using inverse-Hessian estimate, report draws plus ELBO. Cheap, derivative-, embarrassingly parallel – meant HMC warm-start, initialiser imh_laplace(), quick sanity check Laplace approximation. implementation single-path . full multi-path Pathfinder (K parallel L-BFGS runs + mixture proposal + Pareto- smoothed importance reweighting) follow-. single-path version users want Laplace-equivalent diagnostic.

code: install.packages(c("ggplot2", "stars", "sf"))

title: Plot spatial predictions as a map — plot_map
code: # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(123)   n_sites <- 20   df <- data.frame(     y = rbinom(n_sites, 20, 0.4),     elevation = rnorm(n_sites),     site = factor(seq_len(n_sites)),     lon = runif(n_sites),     lat = runif(n_sites)   )   adj <- matrix(0, n_sites, n_sites)   for (i in 1:(n_sites - 1)) adj[i, i + 1] <- adj[i + 1, i] <- 1   fit <- tulpa(     y ~ elevation + spatial(site),     data = df,     family = "binomial",     n_trials = rep(20L, n_sites),     spatial = spatial_car(adj, group_var = "site"),     mode = "laplace"   )   # Areal (CAR/ICAR) fits carry no point coordinates, so pass `coords`:   cc <- df[, c("lon", "lat")]   plot_map(fit, coords = cc)                      # fitted response surface   plot_map(fit, what = "uncertainty", coords = cc)   plot_map_panel(fit, coords = cc)                # both side by side }  # }

title: Predict at new covariate values (population level) — predict.tulpa_fit
text: Prediction linear predictor newdata, link response scale. fixed-effect part X beta credible bounds fixed-effect covariance (vcov()). fit carrying continuous spatial field, posterior-mean field interpolated (kriged) newdata coordinates added linear predictor default, predict() gives conditional (location-specific) prediction. Three continuous field families supported: SPDE Matern field (spatial_spde()), projected mesh; Hilbert-space GP field (spatial_gp(approx = "hsgp")), Laplacian basis re-evaluated new coordinates (training centring / boundary); GP / NNGP field (spatial_gp()), interpolated NNGP conditional mean new location's nearest training locations. HSGP GP/NNGP fields marginalised hyperparameter grid (plugged posterior mean). Ordinary random effects held zero (population level); add group effects ranef() needed.

NULL, predicts training design (requires $model_matrix). type "link" (linear predictor) "response" (mean scale). binomial fit "response" scale per-trial success probability g^{-1}(eta) (n_trials newdata); differs fitted(), returns trial-scaled expected count training design. se.fit TRUE, also return link-scale standard error credible bounds. included SPDE field SE propagates joint (fixed-effect, field) posterior precision fitted hyperparameters – including cross term – conditional (range, sigma) (nested fit's hyperparameter-grid spread propagated, bound mildly optimistic posterior wide). Integer-nu, -RE SPDE fits ; layouts decline explanation. level Credible-interval level (default 0.95). include_field continuous-spatial fit (SPDE, HSGP, GP/NNGP), add kriged field prediction (default TRUE). FALSE gives fixed-effect (population) prediction. Ignored fits continuous field. HSGP GP/NNGP fit field added point prediction uncertainty yet propagated se.fit (interval reflects fixed-effect covariance ). ... Ignored.

title: Show default priors for a tulpa family — priors_default
text: Default priors tulpa follow principles: Fixed effects (beta): Normal(0, 2.5) - weakly informative, allows coefficients roughly [-5, 5] link scale. Random effect SD (sigma): PC prior P(sigma > 1) = 0.01 - favors simpler models smaller variance components. Overdispersion (phi): PC prior P(phi > 10) = 0.01 NB2 size phi (larger phi less overdispersion; phi -> Inf Poisson limit). default keeps phi finite, allowing overdispersion penalising extreme values. Temporal correlation (rho): Beta(2, 2) - symmetric prior centered 0.5, appropriate AR(1) correlation. Spatial mixing (rho_spatial): Beta(1, 1) = Uniform(0, 1) - prior preference structured vs. unstructured spatial variation.

title: Show default priors for a tulpa family — priors_default
code: # Defaults for all families (no family argument) priors_default() #> Default priors for tulpa models #> ================================ #>  #> These defaults apply to all families unless overridden. #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0, 2.5) #>   Interpretation: Coefficients roughly in [-5, 5] on link scale #>   Customization: prior_normal(mean, sd) #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(sigma > 1) = 0.01 #>   Interpretation: Favors smaller variance components #>   Customization: prior_pc(U, alpha) or prior_half_normal(sd) #>  #> Overdispersion (phi) [negbin/poisson_gamma only]: #>   PC prior: P(phi > 10) = 0.01 #>   Interpretation: NB2 size; keeps phi finite (allows overdispersion), #>                   phi -> Inf is the Poisson limit #>   Customization: prior_pc(U, alpha) or prior_gamma(shape, rate) #>  #> Family-specific notes: #>   negbin_negbin: Uses phi for both processes #>   binomial: No overdispersion parameter (unless beta_binomial) #>   poisson_gamma: Uses phi for gamma shape parameter  # Family-specific defaults take a tulpa_family object. Model packages # (e.g. tulpaRatio) register rich families; a minimal one is enough here. fam <- tulpa_family(   name = "poisson_gamma",   simulate_fn = function(eta, params, n_obs, ...) rpois(n_obs, exp(eta[[1]])) ) priors_default(fam) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   )  # Including spatial parameters priors_default(fam, spatial = TRUE) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> Spatial mixing (rho_spatial): #>   Beta(1.00, 1.00)  [mean = 0.50] #>   Used for: BYM2 mixing proportion (structured vs. unstructured) #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   )  # Use as a starting point for customization my_priors <- priors_default(fam) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   ) my_priors$beta <- prior_normal(0, 1)  # Tighter prior on fixed effects

what: Build a prior list for tulpa_nested_laplace() from a tulpa spec object — prior_from_spec
title: Build a prior list for tulpa_nested_laplace() from a tulpa spec object — prior_from_spec
text: Validates tulpa_temporal tulpa_spatial specification data, converts prior list shape consumed tulpa_nested_laplace(). Mainly internal helper callers already fitted spec; users typically pass spec + data directly tulpa_nested_laplace() instead. Supported spec types: tulpa_temporal type {"rw1", "rw2", "ar1"} tulpa_spatial, areal type {"car", "icar", "car_proper", "bym2"}. areal spec returns graph fields – type, spatial_idx, n_spatial_units, adj_row_ptr, adj_col_idx, n_neighbors – plus scale_factor bym2 eigenvalue-derived rho_bounds proper CAR. grid field returned areal type: outer axes built later family's registry defaults() closure, proper CAR's (tau, rho) grid built bounds. tulpa_gp / tulpa_hsgp, continuous type {"gp", "nngp", "hsgp"}: validated data routed nngp / hsgp nested kernel shared converter. SPDE one continuous field built – carries (range, sigma) FEM integrator; call fit_spde() spatial_spde() spec.

title: Random-effect summaries — ranef
text: backend reports group effect follows computes: Sampler tier RE-covariance Gibbs debias (tulpa_re_cov_gibbs(), reached tulpa(..., control = list(re_cov = "gibbs"))) draw random effects jointly everything else, estimate / sd / bounds empirical posterior summaries. RE-covariance integrator (tulpa_re_cov_nested()) carries Gaussian per-group posterior Sigma node; reported summaries exact moments quantiles weighted mixture , carry within-node curvature Sigma uncertainty. group effect subspace debias selected (control$subspace_debias) moved Metropolis sampler every node instead, reported draws. Laplace tier reports conditional mode spread (sd bounds NA), per-group quantity forms. source column says per row produced : "sampled" posterior draw summary, "mixture" node mixture, "mode" conditional mode. fit whose backend never forms per-group posterior (adaptive Gauss-Hermite inner marginal integrates group quadrature) errors reason rather returning empty table, indistinguishable model random effects. model genuinely none returns zero-row data frame.

code: # A conjugate normal-normal model, whose posterior is exact, so its PIT must # be uniform: the harness scoring itself. sim <- function(seed) {   set.seed(seed)   mu <- rnorm(1)   list(y = rnorm(10L, mu, 1), theta = c(mu = mu)) } fitter <- function(d) {   v <- 1 / (1 + length(d$y))   list(exact  = list(mu = sbc_normal(v * sum(d$y), sqrt(v))),        narrow = list(mu = sbc_normal(v * sum(d$y), sqrt(v) / 2))) } res <- sbc("prior_predictive", simulator = sim, fitter = fitter, n_sim = 60L) res #> Simulation-based calibration -- prior_predictive, 60 simulations #>   band: 0.95 simultaneous (equal local levels, exact crossing probability) #>   CRPS: proper posterior score #>   proper prior: verified over 10 probed simulations #>  #>     arm quantity  n     ks inside   p_unif inside_folded p_folded    crps #>   exact       mu 60 0.1239   TRUE 1.72e-01          TRUE    0.466 0.19496 #>  narrow       mu 60 0.2662  FALSE 1.22e-15         FALSE    0.000 0.21762 #>  crps_se #>   0.0166 #>   0.0215 #>  #> 1 of 2 (arm, quantity) reads inside the band; outside the band: narrow/mu. summary(res, baseline = "exact") #> Simulation-based calibration -- prior_predictive, 60 simulations #>   CRPS: proper posterior score #>  #>     arm quantity  n     ks inside   p_unif inside_folded p_folded    crps #>   exact       mu 60 0.1239   TRUE 1.72e-01          TRUE    0.466 0.19496 #>  narrow       mu 60 0.2662  FALSE 1.22e-15         FALSE    0.000 0.21762 #>  crps_se #>   0.0166 #>   0.0215 #>  #> Paired CRPS against arm 'exact' (negative delta = better) #>  quantity    arm  n   delta   t worse_frac p_sign #>        mu narrow 60 0.02267 4.3      0.633 0.0519 #>   delta with its t is the proper-score verdict; p_sign is a more #>   powerful detector of a difference but is not itself proper.

title: Multi-Scale Gaussian Process spatial structure — spatial_multiscale
text: multi-scale model decomposes spatial variation additively: $$\eta(s) = X\beta + w_{local}(s) + w_{regional}(s)$$ component follows independent Gaussian process: $$w_{local}(s) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2_{local} C(\phi_{local}))$$ $$w_{regional}(s) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2_{regional} C(\phi_{regional}))$$ Identifiability: sufficient data (>500 locations), two scales typically well-identified prior ranges non-overlapping. PC priors variance components help prevent overfitting. Computational cost: Approximately 1.5-2x cost single-scale GP, two NNGP likelihoods must evaluated.

title: Multi-Scale Gaussian Process spatial structure — spatial_multiscale
code: # Create multi-scale spatial structure ms <- spatial_multiscale(   ~ lon + lat,   range_local = c(0.1, 0.5),   range_regional = c(1, 5) ) print(ms) #> tulpa Multi-Scale spatial specification #> ======================================== #>  #> Coordinates: lon, lat  #> Scales: local + regional  #>  #> Local scale: #>   Range prior: [0.1, 0.5] #>   Neighbors: 10  #>  #> Regional scale: #>   Range prior: [1, 5] #>   Neighbors: 30  #>  #> Covariance: exponential  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)   # \donttest{ set.seed(101) n <- 25 df <- data.frame(   lon = runif(n, 0, 10),   lat = runif(n, 0, 10),   depth = rnorm(n),   temp = rnorm(n) ) df$count <- rpois(n, exp(1 + 0.2 * df$depth))  # Both scales are sampled by exact NUTS (mode = "exact"); the field is # returned as gp_local[i] / gp_regional[i] draws. fit <- tulpa(   count ~ depth + temp,   data = df,   family = "poisson",   spatial = spatial_multiscale(     ~ lon + lat,     range_local = c(0.1, 0.5),     range_regional = c(1, 5),     nn_local = 5L,     nn_regional = 8L   ),   mode = "exact",   control = list(n_iter = 60L, n_warmup = 30L, seed = 1L) ) summary(fit) #>               estimate std.error        2.5%     97.5% #> (Intercept) 0.94597840 0.3710487  0.15697851 1.5176985 #> depth       0.22858182 0.1292459  0.01878731 0.4725801 #> temp        0.04685671 0.1172341 -0.18428174 0.2186235 # }

code: # Create RSR spatial structure rsr <- spatial_rsr(   spatial_gp(~ lon + lat),   restrict_to = ~ depth + temp ) print(rsr) #> tulpa Gaussian Process spatial specification #> ============================================= #>  #> Coordinates: lon, lat  #> Covariance: exponential  #> Neighbors (NNGP): 15  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  #>  #> Restricted Spatial Regression (RSR): #>   Orthogonal to: ~depth + temp  #>   (Spatial effect constrained to be orthogonal to covariate space)  # \donttest{ # Areal binomial data on a chain of regions, covariate spatially confounded set.seed(404) n_regions <- 12 W <- matrix(0, n_regions, n_regions) for (i in 1:(n_regions - 1)) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1 df <- data.frame(region = factor(rep(1:n_regions, each = 5))) df$x <- as.integer(df$region) / 4 + rnorm(nrow(df), 0, 0.5) df$y <- rbinom(nrow(df), 20, plogis(-0.5 + 0.6 * df$x))  # RSR orthogonalises the spatial field to x, protecting its coefficient fit <- tulpa(   y ~ x + spatial(region),   data = df,   family = "binomial",   n_trials = rep(20L, nrow(df)),   spatial = spatial_rsr(spatial_car(W, level = "obs"), restrict_to = ~ x),   mode = "auto",   control = list(n_iter = 500L, warmup = 250L) ) summary(fit) #>               estimate  std.error       2.5%       97.5% #> (Intercept) -0.3172248 0.11295433 -0.5502363 -0.09914267 #> x            0.5278281 0.06516213  0.4022617  0.65216922 # }

title: Spatiotemporal interaction specifications for tulpa — spatiotemporal
text: Spatiotemporal interactions extend basic additive model: $$\eta_{st} = X\beta + f_s(space) + f_t(time)$$ include interactions: $$\eta_{st} = X\beta + f_s(space) + f_t(time) + \delta_{st}$$ \(\delta_{st}\) captures space-time interactions. Interaction Types (following Knorr-Held, 2000): Type : Unstructured interaction - IID \(\delta_{st} \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\) Type II: Structured time, unstructured space - temporal structure location Type III: Structured space, unstructured time - spatial structure time Type IV: Structured space time - full Kronecker interaction Separable Models: Separable: Covariance Kronecker product \(C_{st} = C_s \otimes C_t\) Non-separable: GP joint space-time metric Type (IID) Independent random effect space-time combination: $$\delta_{st} \stackrel{iid}{\sim} N(0, \sigma^2_\delta)$$ simplest form, requiring S*T parameters capturing structured interaction. Type II (Temporal structure per location) location temporal random effect: $$\delta_{\cdot t}^{(s)} \sim RW(\sigma^2)$$ captures location-specific temporal trends assumes independence across locations. Type III (Spatial structure per time point) time point spatial random effect: $$\delta_{s \cdot}^{(t)} \sim ICAR(\tau)$$ captures time-specific spatial patterns assumes independence across time points. Type IV (Full structure) Kronecker product spatial temporal precision matrices: $$Q_\delta = Q_s \otimes Q_t$$ constrained model, assuming interaction structure marginal effects. Separable GP-based effects, assumes separable covariance: $$C(\mathbf{s}_1, t_1; \mathbf{s}_2, t_2) = C_s(\mathbf{s}_1, \mathbf{s}_2) \cdot C_t(t_1, t_2)$$

stationary autoregressive process order p, \(w_t = \sum_{j=1}^{p} \phi_j w_{t-j} + \varepsilon_t\), user-defined GMRF latent block model formula via latent(temporal_ar(...)) – general-order extension temporal_ar2(), sharing construction: precision exact stationary AR(p) GMRF (banded inverse Yule-Walker Toeplitz autocovariance), stationarity enforced partial-autocorrelation parameterization (Levinson-Durbin map p unconstrained atanh_psi hyperparameters), hyperparameter integration never leaves stationary region. block's hyperparameters log_tau (log innovation precision) atanh_psi1..atanh_psi

Can formula (e.g., ~ year) character string (e.g., "year"). numeric (continuous time) convertible numeric. cov Covariance function: "exponential" (default, rough), "matern" (tunable smoothness), "gaussian" (smooth), "periodic" (seasonal patterns). nu Smoothness parameter Matern covariance, one : 0.5: equivalent exponential (rough) 1.5: differentiable (moderate smoothness) 2.5: twice differentiable (smooth) smoothnesses closed form; anything needs Bessel function second kind rejected. Ignored non-Matern covariance functions. period Period periodic covariance (e.g., 12 monthly, 365 daily data annual cycle). used cov = "periodic". group_var Optional name grouping variable panel data. provided, separate GPs estimated group. shared Logical; TRUE (default), temporal effect enters processes. scale_coords Logical; TRUE (default), time values scaled unit variance computing distances. parameterization Parameterization GP effects: "noncentered" (default) stores z ~ N(0,1) scales covariance (better weakly-informed effects); "centered" stores effects directly (better strongly-informed effects).

title: Gaussian Process temporal structure — temporal_gp
text: GP temporal model adds time-correlated random effect: $$\eta(t) = X\beta + f(t)$$ \(f(t)\) follows Gaussian process: $$f(t) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2 C(|t - t'|; \phi))$$ correlation function \(C(d; \phi)\) depends time distance \(d\): Exponential: \(C(d) = \exp(-d/\phi)\) - continuous differentiable Matern: Smooth tunable roughness via \(\nu\) Gaussian: \(C(d) = \exp(-(d/\phi)^2)\) - infinitely differentiable Periodic: \(C(d) = \exp(-2\sin^2(\pi d/p)/\phi^2)\) - seasonal data Implementation: exponential kernel (equivalently Matern nu = 0.5) Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, joint density factorizes first-order Markov chain evaluates O(T) matrix. kernels finite-dimensional state-space form evaluated dense T x T Cholesky, T number distinct time points. field fit sampler path: two hyperparameters (log_sigma2_temporal_gp, logit_phi_temporal_gp) sampled jointly field fixed effects, pass sampler mode mode = "hmc". nested-Laplace kernel .

title: Gaussian Process temporal structure — temporal_gp
code: # Create GP temporal specification temporal_gp("timestamp") #> tulpa Gaussian Process temporal specification #> ============================================== #>  #> Time variable: timestamp  #> Covariance: exponential  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  temporal_gp("day", cov = "matern", nu = 1.5) #> tulpa Gaussian Process temporal specification #> ============================================== #>  #> Time variable: day  #> Covariance: matern (nu = 1.5)  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  temporal_gp("month", cov = "periodic", period = 12) #> tulpa Gaussian Process temporal specification #> ============================================== #>  #> Time variable: month  #> Covariance: periodic (period = 12.0)  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)   # \donttest{ # Irregularly-spaced time series set.seed(140) times <- sort(runif(40, 0, 10)) df <- data.frame(   time = times,   x = rnorm(40),   y = rbinom(40, 1, 0.5) )  fit <- tulpa(   y ~ x,   data = df,   family = "binomial",   temporal = temporal_gp("time"),   mode = "hmc",   control = list(n_iter = 200, warmup = 100, n_chains = 1) ) # }

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
text: Q function function(theta) returning sparse precision matrix class Matrix::sparseMatrix (typically dgCMatrix). matrix must square symmetric. Called registration theta = init infer n_latent capture sparsity pattern. prior function function(theta) returning finite numeric scalar – log-prior density theta. init Numeric vector starting values theta. Names, present, become canonical theta names. mu Optional function function(theta) returning numeric vector length n_latent. Default NULL equivalent zero mean. graph Optional sparse matrix specifying upper bound Q's sparsity pattern. supplied, registration check verifies nonzero pattern Q(init) subset. bounds Optional list components lower upper, numeric vector length length(init). Used nested_laplace + CCD build outer grid; unused NUTS / VI. obs_idx Optional integer vector mapping observation latent slot [1, n_latent]. NULL (default), fit-time driver assumes N == n_latent uses seq_len(N) – .e. one observation per latent slot, row order. name Optional character; cosmetic label used print() / summary().

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
text: object class c("tgmrf", "tulpa_latent_block") components: Q, prior, mu – user closures (NULL mu). init, theta_names, theta_dim – hyperparameter metadata. n_latent – inferred Q(init). pattern – captured sparsity pattern dgCMatrix 1s. graph – user-supplied pattern, validated pattern given. bounds, name – passed .

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
text: Gaussian latent block z ~ N(mu(theta), Q(theta)^{-1}): $$\log p(z\mid\theta) = \tfrac{1}{2}\log\det Q(\theta) - \tfrac{1}{2}(z - \mu(\theta))^\top Q(\theta)(z - \mu(\theta)) + \mathrm{const}$$ gradient -Q(z - mu) Hessian -Q wrt z closed form, user never writes gradient code. Laplace inner step needs Q(theta) mu(theta) numeric theta. NUTS VI additionally use forward finite-difference gradient theta, costing dim(theta) extra Q calls per outer step – cheap typical dim(theta) <= 5.

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
code: # Periodic AR(1) block, wrap-around tridiagonal precision. periodic_ar1 <- function(n) {   tgmrf(     Q = function(theta) {       sigma <- exp(theta[1]); rho <- tanh(theta[2])       d <- rep((1 + rho^2) / sigma^2, n)       o <- rep(-rho / sigma^2, n)       M <- Matrix::bandSparse(         n, k = c(-1, 0, 1), diagonals = list(o, d, o)       )       M[1, n] <- M[n, 1] <- -rho / sigma^2       methods::as(M, "CsparseMatrix")     },     prior = function(theta) {       stats::dnorm(theta[1], 0, 1, log = TRUE) +         stats::dnorm(theta[2], 0, 1, log = TRUE)     },     init = c(log_sigma = 0, atanh_rho = 0),     name = "periodic_ar1"   ) }  blk <- periodic_ar1(20) print(blk) #> <tgmrf> "periodic_ar1" #>   n_latent : 20 #>   theta    : 2 dim (log_sigma, atanh_rho) #>   init     : 0, 0 #>   Q nnz    : 20 (5% of dense) #>   backend  : r

what: tulpa: Templated Unified Library for Posterior Approximation in Bayesian Hierarchical Models — tulpa-package
title: tulpa: Templated Unified Library for Posterior Approximation in Bayesian Hierarchical Models — tulpa-package
text: general-purpose engine fitting Bayesian hierarchical models spatial fields, temporal effects, spatially varying coefficients, multiple inference backends. Scalable spatial structure includes Hilbert space approximate Gaussian processes (HSGP; Riutort-Mayol et al. 2023 doi:10.1007/s11222-022-10167-2 ), nearest-neighbor Gaussian processes (NNGP; Datta et al. 2016 doi:10.1080/01621459.2015.1044091 ), intrinsic conditional autoregressive models (ICAR; Besag, York, Mollie 1991 doi:10.1007/BF00116466 ), reparameterized Besag-York-Mollie model (BYM2; Riebler et al. 2016 doi:10.1177/0962280216660421 ), stochastic partial differential equation fields (SPDE; Lindgren, Rue, Lindstrom 2011 doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2011.00777.x ). Temporal structure covers random walks, autoregressive processes, Gaussian processes. Inference tiered correctness guarantee: exact Hamiltonian Monte Carlo -U-Turn sampler, Laplace nested Laplace approximations hyperparameter integration (Rue, Martino, Chopin 2009 doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00700.x ), variational inference. Model-specific packages plug observation likelihoods engine templated C++ callback interface.

Categorical families take fixed-effect models . mode Inference mode backend. "auto" (default) picks reliable Tier 1/Tier 2 method expected finish; tier ("exact", "structured") backend name ("laplace", "mala", ...) forces . "eb" estimates random-effect covariance(s) empirical Bayes instead conditioning sigma_re (see tulpa_eb()); opt-name, intervals conditional estimate rather marginal . sigma_re Random-effect SDs condition : length 1 (recycled) one per RE term. Defaults 1 per term message. Ignored backends determine covariance ("eb", re_cov_nested, re_cov_gibbs, gibbs, agq), warn supplied anyway. n_trials Binomial denominators (length nrow(data)), NULL. weights Optional observation weights (non-negative numeric vector, length nrow(data)): observation's log-likelihood contribution scaled weight (prior / frequency weights, e.g. survey weights aggregated-data counts – weight 2 equivalent duplicating row). Supported non-spatial Laplace path (mode = "laplace") log-posterior samplers (mala, imh_laplace, pathfinder); backends reject weights loudly. phi Dispersion/precision passed family (residual variance gaussian lognormal, size neg_binomial_2, precision beta, scale t). variance convention holds across every backend; SD-parameterized compiled kernels receive sqrt(phi) boundary. estimate_phi Estimate dispersion data instead conditioning phi, supplies starting value. log(phi) joins empirical-Bayes maximization one coordinate carrying exact derivative Laplace log-marginal, estimate ML-II: hyperprior covers random-effect covariances dispersion enters unpenalized. fit$phi estimate fit$phi_estimated distinguishes conditioned value. Available mode = "eb", families whose dispersion derivative registered (see tulpa_eb()). mode errors rather fitting starting value name says otherwise. phi2 Optional second dispersion: Student-t degrees freedom (family = "t"; default 4 NULL) Tweedie variance power (family = "tweedie", required – defaulted power statistical decision caller never made). Supported non-spatial Laplace path, random-effect covariance paths (mode = "eb" nested Sigma integrator, thread inner Laplace solve), log-posterior samplers, ModelData samplers. Backends without phi2 channel refuse rather fit family's default. estimate_phi covers phi alone; phi2 always conditioned . beta_prior Optional list(mean, sd) Gaussian prior fixed effects. Backends carry mixture refuse rather fit model without . zi_prior Optional list(sd) Gaussian prior zero-inflation coefficients, beta_zi ~ N(0, sd^2); NULL (default) uses 2.5. One scalar SD applies whole block, mean fixed 0, compiled kernels carry. prior identifies logit level contributes zeros – likelihood monotone coefficient alone send -Inf. sd = Inf removes penalty. Ignored without ziformula. warm_start Optional starting point NUTS sampler, cheaper fit model: "eb" "laplace" fits one first, pass existing fit either mode. sampler starts mode inverse mass read curvature, instead origin structural one. Chains first dispersed around mode fit's scale, -chain spread – rhat() compares – collapsed shared starting point. PSIS-LOO reuses native tulpa_psis() smoothing, CPO LOO numbers computation (CPO_i = exp(elpd_loo_i), LPML = elpd_loo). input may matrix streaming tulpa_loglik() EVA-scale fits processed observation blocks.

title: Model criteria from a pointwise log-likelihood — tulpa_criteria
text: log_lik [n_draws x n_obs] numeric matrix pointwise log-likelihoods, tulpa_loglik() streaming wrapper. criteria criteria compute. "waic", "loo", "cpo", "lpml", "dic". "loo", "cpo", "lpml" share single PSIS pass; "dic" additionally needs loglik_at_mean. loglik_at_mean Optional length-n_obs vector pointwise log-likelihoods evaluated posterior mean parameters, supplied caller (model package knows parameterization). Required DIC's plug-deviance; without DIC fields NA. group Optional length-n_obs grouping (integer / factor / character vector). LOO unit one column log_lik: group = NULL (default) every column fold (leave-one-row-, e.g. per plot / per visit) result byte-identical ungrouped call. supplied, per-draw pointwise log-likelihoods summed within group [n_draws x n_groups] matrix PSIS, fold whole group (leave-one-group-cross-validation, LOGO-CV). Use switch estimand per-row per-group LOO – e.g. cell-compressed hierarchical fit, leave whole cell rather one rows. WAIC's variance term, lppd, elpd_loo, cpo pareto_k computed grouped matrix. DIC plug-deviance observations unaffected group. chunk_size Number observation columns process per block. default streams whole matrix materialized, else picks block sized million entries. pointwise TRUE, also return per-observation vectors (elpd_waic, p_waic, elpd_loo, pareto_k, cpo) plotting / stacking.

LOO unit whatever one column log_lik holds. consumer built matrix one column per row (plot / visit), default per-row LOO; column already carries whole group's compressed likelihood, leaving drops group pareto_k can blow construction. group argument makes unit explicit: supply aggregate columns folds report leave-one-group-CV (LOGO-CV) instead, different deliberate estimand.

title: Model criteria from a pointwise log-likelihood — tulpa_criteria
code: # A draws x observations log-likelihood matrix (here built directly; # in practice extracted from a fitted model's posterior draws). set.seed(1) y  <- rnorm(40) mu <- matrix(rnorm(200 * 40, sd = 0.2), 200, 40) ll <- dnorm(matrix(y, 200, 40, byrow = TRUE), mean = mu, log = TRUE) tulpa_criteria(ll) #> tulpa model criteria  (200 draws x 40 observations) #>   WAIC           107.7  (SE 7.3) #>   elpd_waic      -53.9  (SE 3.7) #>   p_waic           1.4  (SE 0.3) #>   LOOIC          107.8  (SE 7.3) #>   elpd_loo       -53.9  (SE 3.7) #>   p_loo            1.4 #>   LPML           -53.9 #>   DIC               NA #>   p_DIC             NA tulpa_criteria(ll, criteria = "waic", pointwise = TRUE)$pointwise[1:3, ] #>   obs       lppd  elpd_waic      p_waic #> 1   1 -1.1272129 -1.1439778 0.016764831 #> 2   2 -0.9525029 -0.9546593 0.002156456 #> 3   3 -1.2680835 -1.3033304 0.035246901

what: Soft latent labels go in weights, not in y
title: Fit a latent-variable model via EM + Laplace approximation — tulpa_em_laplace
text: M-step maximizes expected complete-data log-likelihood. Bernoulli latent z_i carrying E-step posterior weight w_i $$Q = \sum_i [\, w_i \log p_i + (1 - w_i) \log (1 - p_i) \,],$$ weighted Bernoulli log-likelihood, carries binomial coefficient. Encode two rows per unit – y = 1 weight w_i y = 0 weight 1 - w_i: fractional y binomial block refused, objective: asks exact binomial density non-integer response, whose normalizer lchoose(n, y) zero depends w. weighted encoding block's log_marginal Laplace marginal Q, EM objective increases across iterations.
code: list(y       = rep(c(1, 0), each = n),      X       = rbind(X, X),      weights = c(w, 1 - w),      family  = "binomial")

title: Fit a latent-variable model via EM + Laplace approximation — tulpa_em_laplace
code: # \donttest{ # Zero-inflated Poisson via EM: the E-step scores the posterior probability # that each zero is non-structural. Those are soft labels, so the occupancy # arm is the weighted Bernoulli above -- two rows per unit -- and the # abundance arm weights each count by the same w. set.seed(1) n <- 200 z <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.7) y <- rpois(n, 4) * z X <- cbind(1, rnorm(n))  e_step <- function(fits, ...) {   if (!length(fits)) return(list(weights = pmax(as.numeric(y > 0), 0.5)))   psi <- plogis(drop(X %*% fits$occ$mode))   lam <- exp(drop(X %*% fits$abund$mode))   w <- ifelse(y > 0, 1, psi * exp(-lam) / (psi * exp(-lam) + (1 - psi)))   list(weights = w) } m_step_encode <- function(weights, ...) {   list(     occ   = list(y = rep(c(1, 0), each = n), X = rbind(X, X),                  weights = c(weights, 1 - weights), family = "binomial"),     abund = list(y = y, X = X, family = "poisson", weights = weights)   ) }  res <- tulpa_em_laplace(e_step, m_step_encode, verbose = FALSE) res$converged #> [1] TRUE plogis(res$fits$occ$mode[1])    # P(non-structural), truth 0.7 #> [1] 0.7041959 exp(res$fits$abund$mode[1])     # abundance mean, truth 4 #> [1] 3.872501 # }

title: Nested Laplace approximation for latent Gaussian models — tulpa_nested_laplace
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) S <- 30L                                   # spatial units arranged in a chain nb <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) setdiff(c(s - 1L, s + 1L), c(0L, S + 1L))) nn <- lengths(nb) field <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(S, 0, 0.4))))   # smooth spatial field idx <- rep(seq_len(S), each = 6L); n <- length(idx); x <- rnorm(n) y <- rbinom(n, 1L, plogis(-0.2 + 0.6 * x + field[idx])) prior <- list(type = "icar", n_spatial_units = S, spatial_idx = idx,               adj_row_ptr = c(0L, cumsum(nn)), adj_col_idx = unlist(nb) - 1L,               n_neighbors = nn, tau_grid = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)) fit <- tulpa_nested_laplace(y, rep(1L, n), cbind(1, x), prior = prior,                             family = "binomial") fit$theta_mean        # marginalized ICAR precision #> [1] 5.742009 # }

Supported priors: "bym2"       – outer grid (sigma, rho [, alpha]). Latent: phi (n_s) | theta (n_s) unit-precision ICAR + iid components. "icar"       – outer grid (sigma [, alpha]). Latent: phi (n_s) unit-precision ICAR. "car_proper" – outer grid (sigma, rho_car [, alpha]). Latent: phi (n_s) Q = D - rho_car * W. backends (NNGP, HSGP, RW1/2, AR1) follow interface land Phase 3.

title: Joint multi-likelihood nested Laplace approximation — tulpa_nested_laplace_joint
text: arm's linear predictor reads $$\eta_{arm} = X_{arm} \beta_{arm} + \sigma_{arm} \cdot z_s,$$ \(z_s\) unit-precision latent (ICAR(tau=1) ICAR/BYM2, BYM2 mix; CAR_proper uses structure \(D - \rho_{car} W\)). arms share donor amplitude \(\sigma\) outer-grid sigma_grid axis. copy arm's amplitude \(\sigma_{arm} = \alpha \cdot \sigma\), \(\alpha\) direct outer-grid axis taken copy$alpha_grid. Cartesian product (sigma, [rho/rho_car,] alpha[, phi]). Direct \(\alpha\) outer-grid axis (rather post-hoc ratio \(\alpha = \sigma_{pos} / \sigma_{occ}\)) avoids plug-bias weakly-identified ratio small n_pos lets regularizing hyperprior land \(\alpha\) directly.

title: Joint multi-likelihood nested Laplace approximation — tulpa_nested_laplace_joint
text: Rue, Martino & Chopin (2009). Approximate Bayesian inference latent Gaussian models using integrated nested Laplace approximations. JRSS-B 71(2):319-392.

title: Joint multi-likelihood nested Laplace approximation — tulpa_nested_laplace_joint
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) S <- 25L                                   # shared spatial units (chain graph) nb <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) setdiff(c(s - 1L, s + 1L), c(0L, S + 1L))) nn <- lengths(nb) field <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(S, 0, 0.4)))) mk_arm <- function(m, fam) {   si <- sample(S, m, replace = TRUE); x <- rnorm(m)   lin <- 0.2 + 0.5 * x + 0.8 * field[si]   y <- if (fam == "binomial") rbinom(m, 1L, plogis(lin)) else lin + rnorm(m, 0, 0.5)   list(y = as.numeric(y), n_trials = rep(1L, m), X = cbind(1, x),        spatial_idx = si, family = fam, phi = if (fam == "gaussian") 0.5 else 1) } prior <- list(type = "icar", n_spatial_units = S,               adj_row_ptr = c(0L, cumsum(nn)), adj_col_idx = unlist(nb) - 1L,               n_neighbors = nn, sigma_grid = c(0.3, 0.7, 1.4)) fit <- tulpa_nested_laplace_joint(   responses = list(occ = mk_arm(200L, "binomial"), pos = mk_arm(200L, "gaussian")),   prior = prior) #> [nested-laplace-joint] 1/3 cells (33%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace-joint] 3/3 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells fit$theta_mean        # shared field amplitude, integrated across both arms #>     sigma  #> 0.3147239  # }

title: Fit a beta-regression model via NUTS (joint sampling of beta + log_phi) — tulpa_nuts_beta
text: Bayesian counterpart tulpa_laplace_beta(). Routes Beta GLM tulpa's full NUTS backend via generic LikelihoodSpec interface, sampling precision phi jointly regression coefficients log scale. NUTS performs exact marginalisation phi, replacing Brent outer-opt tulpa_laplace_beta() deterministic nested-Laplace grid otherwise integrate Beta dispersion. Mean-precision parameterisation, default logit link: y_i ~ Beta(mu_i * phi, (1 - mu_i) * phi) mu_i = 1 / (1 + exp(-eta_i)) eta_i = X_i %*% beta.

title: Sample an SPDE GLM via NUTS, optionally jointly over Matern hypers — tulpa_nuts_spde
text: Bayesian counterpart fit_spde() / laplace_spde_at(). Routes SPDE-augmented GLM tulpa's full NUTS backend via generic LikelihoodSpec interface. Two modes: Legacy / fixed-hyper (joint = FALSE, default): conditions supplied (range, sigma). Samples latent block (beta, w_mesh, log_phi) jointly. Useful inner step outer CCD / nested-Laplace integration hypers. Joint hypers (joint = TRUE): samples (beta, z_mesh, log_kappa, log_tau, log_phi) jointly via non-centered transform w = L(theta)^{-T} z. PC prior (Fuglstad et al. 2019 JASA) (range, sigma) taken prior_range, prior_sigma. Returns additional w_draws, range_draws, sigma_draws, kappa_draws, tau_draws columns/vectors top raw parameter draws.

title: Adaptive Gauss-Hermite refinement of a grouped random-effect covariance — tulpa_re_aghq
text: Refines generalized linear mixed model's fixed effects random-effect covariance replacing per-group Laplace integral n_quad-point adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (AGHQ). n_quad = 1 joint Laplace (glmer nAGQ = 1); higher n_quad reduces small-cluster attenuation variance components binary / count data. Unlike agq_fit() (intercept-RE, built-binomial/poisson/gaussian likelihoods), engine callback-driven: caller supplies per-group conditional likelihood, custom marginal (e.g. latent-state-integrated occupancy / detection likelihood, latent-abundance-integrated N-mixture marginal) refines quadrature. engine block, front door: model packages call programmatically, tuning knobs (max_iter, n_quad, keep) sit signature rather control list. engine structure-agnostic. integrates per-group marginal $$M_g = \int \exp\{\ell_g(b_g)\}\, N(b_g; 0, \Sigma)\, db_g,$$ \(b_g\) group's random-effect vector (dimension \(\sum_m c_m\) RE terms) \(\ell_g(b_g)\) group's conditional log-likelihood linear predictors perturbed \(b_g\). \(b_g\) enters likelihood – one linear predictor, several coupled arms different observation granularities (e.g. per-site abundance arm per-visit detection arm sharing species grouping) – lives entirely callback. engine needs, per group, value / gradient / Hessian \(\ell_g\) \(b_g\) (mode) \(\ell_g\) quadrature nodes (sum). fixed parameters theta log-Cholesky coordinates \(\Sigma\) optimized jointly \(\sum_g \log M_g\); standard errors come exact-marginal Hessian. Two callback forms select structure (supply exactly one): make_site – common single-arm, per-row-separable case (\(\ell_g(b_g) = \sum_{\g} \log f_i(\eta_i + Z_i b_g)\) one linear predictor \(\eta\)). engine builds oracle per-row marginal RE design Z . make_group – general / multi-arm case. caller supplies per-group b-space oracle directly, non-separable units (e.g. visits N-mixture site coupled shared latent count) random effects several arms handled engine change. Scope: one shared grouping factor across RE terms (per-group integral factorizes). total RE dimension per group small (quadrature grid n_quad^dim).

RE-arm predictor eta, used per-group mode), lmat = function(rows, ETA) returning length(rows) x ncol(ETA) matrix per-observation log-likelihoods quadrature node columns. Required make_site path; ignored make_group. keep Optional logical/integer mask observations include (default ; make_site path ). Rows outside keep dropped every group. n_quad Quadrature nodes per RE dimension. Either single integer (default 9; 1 = Laplace) broadcast every covariance block, integer vector length length(re_terms) giving per-block node count. tensor grid uses n_quad[b] nodes along every dimension block b, prod_b n_quad[b]^(dim_b) total nodes; scalar reproduces uniform grid exactly. code: # \donttest{ # A per-row-separable binomial GLMM marginal supplied through `make_site`. l1pe <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0, x + log1p(exp(-x)), log1p(exp(x))) make_binom_site <- function(X, y, nt) function(theta) {   eta_fixed <- as.numeric(X %*% theta)   list(eta_re = eta_fixed,        deriv = function(rows, eta) {          p <- plogis(eta)          list(logL = y[rows] * eta - nt[rows] * l1pe(eta),               d1 = y[rows] - nt[rows] * p, d2 = -nt[rows] * p * (1 - p))        },        lmat = function(rows, ETA) y[rows] * ETA - nt[rows] * l1pe(ETA)) } set.seed(1) ng <- 30L; npg <- 8L; n <- ng * npg g <- rep(seq_len(ng), each = npg); x <- rnorm(n) X <- cbind(1, x); nt <- rep(3L, n); u <- rnorm(ng, 0, 0.9) y <- rbinom(n, nt, plogis(0.3 + 0.7 * x + u[g])) fit <- tulpa_re_aghq(theta0 = c(0, 0),                      re_terms = list(list(idx = g, n_groups = ng, n_coefs = 1L)),                      Sigma0 = list(matrix(0.25, 1, 1)),                      make_site = make_binom_site(X, y, nt), n_obs = n, n_quad = 5L) sqrt(fit$Sigma_list[[1]][1, 1])     # adaptive-GHQ RE standard deviation #> [1] 0.796036 # }

title: tulpa 0.0.8 (2026-06-02)
text: feat(nested-laplace): CCD outer integration joint multi-block path (gcol33/tulpa#59). control$integration = "ccd" (default >= 3 transformable axes) integrates joint hyperparameter posterior central composite design around mode – far fewer inner solves k^d tensor product. Besag sum--zero penalty dense rank-1 (1 1') Hessian; sparse path previously stored diagonal, force_sparse / large-field ICAR BYM2 joint fits log-marginal dense path missing rank-1 log-det term. Now exact, size-gated: small fields densify field block store 1 1' directly; large fields fold rank-1 solve time (Sherman-Morrison step + matrix-determinant-lemma log-det) via one reuse-solve per field. title: tulpa 0.0.5
text: feat(nested-laplace): fits now record wall-clock runtime returned object fit$timing (gcol33/tulpa#48). named numeric seconds carrying total plus phase breakdown – setup (validation / encoding / grid construction), grid (inner Laplace solves scale grid size core count, including adaptive-refinement consistency passes), postproc (weight / moment / marginal assembly), diagnostics (outer Pareto-k-hat). Covers tulpa_nested_laplace() (single- multi-block) tulpa_nested_laplace_joint() (single- multi-block dispatch); consumer fits riding joint object inherit . new print method nested-Laplace classes surfaces one-line summary ("fit 5h 25m (grid 2h 09m)") alongside hyperparameters, grid size, outer Pareto-k-hat. perf(nested-laplace): sparse joint outer grid now runs parallel control$n_threads_outer (gcol33/tulpa#46, lever 2). previously forced serial outer loop, large field inner per-observation OpenMP parallelised cores idled. sparse driver now allocates per-outer-thread pool (Hessian builder, Newton scratch, arm specs, scatter index cache, DENSE_BASIS scratch) dispatches grid cells across n_threads_outer, matching dense driver. phi-grid dispersion axis parallel-safe: rewrites shared arms dispersion per cell, cell snapshots thread’s specs short critical lock-free Newton solve. memory guard clamps thread count replicated builders large (wide fields fall back fewer outer threads). Parallel-vs-serial parity (without phi axis) covered tests/testthat/test-nested-laplace-joint-sparse-parallel.R. perf(nested-laplace): grad-inner-Newton steps inner_refresh (gcol33/tulpa#46, lever 1b). factor-reuse step Hessian discarded, cell-coupling scatter now passes grad_only request CellCouplingSpec (new ABI-appended CellDerivs::grad_only): spec may skip negative-Hessian work (e.g. beta arm’s digamma/trigamma) emit exact gradient, kernel skips cross-arm Hessian scatter. Specs implement write full Hessian (correct, saving). gradient stays exact every step, converged mode unchanged – validated grad--honoring cell-coupling reuse test tests/testthat/test-nested-laplace-joint-inner-refresh.R. perf(nested-laplace): control$inner_refresh (default 1L) adds Shamanskii / chord-method Cholesky factor reuse sparse joint inner Newton (gcol33/tulpa#46). non-quadratic positive arm (e.g. beta cover arm) latent Hessian changes every inner iteration, default re-factorizes sparse Cholesky step – dominant per-grid-cell cost. inner_refresh = m > 1 re-factorizes every m-th inner step reuses cached factor (refreshing early reused solve fails). gradient exact every step step line-search safeguarded, converged mode unchanged final mode-pass Hessian (log_det, SEs) always fresh – path mode uses stale curvature. Applies sparse LM path; dense small-n_x path re-factorizes cheaply ignores . Bit-equivalence every-step default covered tests/testthat/test-nested-laplace-joint-inner-refresh.R. feat(nested-laplace): tulpa_posterior_draws(fit, idx, n) – generic posterior sampler grid-integrated joint nested-Laplace backend (inla.posterior.sample() analogue, gcol33/tulpa#44). Draws outer-grid mixture sum_k w_k N(m_k, V_k): draw picks grid cell integration weights, samples inner latent vector cell’s constrained Gaussian via stored sparse precision Q_csc_*_per_grid (requires control$store_Q = TRUE). ICAR / BYM2 field sum--zero constraint imposed conditioning kriging (Rue & Held 2005), per-cell marginal matches constrained inner-Laplace covariance exactly; single-block multi-block (multi-field trend) layouts handled. Sampling mixture – rather single moment-matched Gaussian – faithful primitive marginalizing nonlinear derived quantities (change occupancy, expected-cover products). Draws tagged iid. Tests tests/testthat/test-posterior-draws-joint.R. fix(nested-laplace): joint outer-grid cheap-pass prune (control$prune = TRUE) longer mis-ranks grid cells drops true posterior mode (gcol33/tulpa#43). screen previously ran single Newton step one global pilot mode every cell; inner latent mode moves substantially across outer grid (large spatial fields, wide sigma/rho/alpha ranges) one-step approximation mis-estimated far cells O(1e5) log-units inverted ranking, prune skip full solve actual mode. screen now rank-faithful chained sweep lattice: cell runs short Newton run warm-started previous screened cell’s quasi-mode, every cheap mode stays near cell’s true mode cheap ranking agrees full-solve ranking. fix(nested-laplace): added safety gate joint cheap-pass prune. cheap-screen argmax disagrees full-solve argmax, kept posterior collapses onto cell whose cheap-vs-full log-marginal gap large, fitter warns falls back full grid ($prune_fallback_triggered, $prune_fallback_reason) rather silently returning pruned answer. silently-wrong pruned posterior now impossible. feat(spde): fit_spde() reports outer Pareto-k-hat accuracy diagnostic ($pareto_k) integrated (range, sigma) hyperparameters – iid-fit counterpart Rhat. k-hat < 0.7 means Gaussian proposal integrator orients CCD/grid fits hyperparameter posterior; >= 0.7 flags skewed / heavy-tailed posterior grid misfits. Controlled diagnose_k (default TRUE) / k_samples (default 200), RNG-restored fit’s draws unchanged. feat(nested-laplace): joint backend (tulpa_nested_laplace_joint, single- multi-block) reports outer Pareto-k-hat heterogeneous hyperparameter space (gcol33/tulpa#42). block-type-aware per-axis transform unconstrains axis – positive scales log, BYM2 mixing weight logit, copy coefficient identity – summed log-Jacobians enter importance target. CAR_proper rho_car axis (support adjacency eigenvalue interval, guessable) declines quadrature ESS rather apply wrong transform. feat(nested-laplace): control$hessian selects inner-Newton curvature joint mixture Hessian – "lm" (default, diagonal-ridge escalation CHOLMOD factorizes), "psd" (eigen-clamp dense observed Hessian), "fisher" (complete-data expected information, PSD construction). feat(joint-laplace): cross-arm coupling via CellCouplingSpec registry (gcol33/tulpa#32). Consumer packages register per-cell coupling spec (e.g. tulpaObs’s cover-hurdle) two arms share latent field; cross-arm block assembled joint Hessian (tulpa_register_cell_coupling C callable, default "separable" always available).

title: tulpa 0.0.2

Removed gradient kernels (D-3, ~30 files, ~17 KLOC). hand-coded H-mode kernels (composite + 4 phases, vectorized + 5 fragments, analytical, autodiff, feature, gp, hsgp, msgp, svc, tvc, st, temporal_gp, ms_temporal, latent), collapsed-spatial machinery (hmc_icar_collapsed_* ×9, hmc_gp_collapsed_* ×5), legacy ratio likelihood (hmc_likelihood.h, hmc_observation_likelihood.h), legacy fallback gradients (compute_gradient_numerical / _autodiff / _arena / _forward / _numerical_impl) deleted. 6 log_post_impl_*_block.h fragments 2 Rcpp ModelData populators (model_data_rcpp.h, hmc_modeldata_builders.h) follow. verify_gradient_runtime now always uses compute_gradient_generic_numerical reference. Simplified samplers (D-4). compute_param_layout (src/hmc_param_layout.cpp) requires n_processes > 0; model packages place model-specific scalars (overdispersion etc.) LikelihoodSpec extra-parameter block layout.extra_offset. ESS’s build_gaussian_priors get_non_gaussian_params (src/ess_sampler.h) walk process_beta_start extra_offset . hmc_nuts_mass_init.cpp drops family-specific block-spec heuristics (NB+ICAR / Bin+ICAR forced DENSE, NB phi-pair 2×2 block) — re-introducing need LikelihoodSpec hint. ST_IV mass-matrix override disabled. precision-informed diagonal mass setup warmup end (src/hmc_nuts_chain_iter_nuts.h) reconstructed eta data.legacy.X_num_flat branched legacy ModelType. ST_IV chains now fall back adapted DIAG mass matrix override re-expressed spec->eta_weights_fn. One -op per chain warmup end; practical impact sampling efficiency small. Removed skipped tests. tests/testthat/test-log-post-split.R tests/testthat/test-hmc-modeldata-builders.R deleted (every test Phase-D skip). legacy-ratio gradient-check test test-spatial-car-proper.R removed; two R-side spatial_car_proper() construction tests stay. Cumulative numbers. Phase D-1..D-5 deletes ~57 files ~18 000 lines legacy ratio infrastructure across src/, inst/include/tulpa/, tests/, tools/. Net code reduction v13 maintenance window starts. Downstream rebuild notes: * tulpaRatio already routes generic LikelihoodSpec path via tulpa_bridge.cpp + per-family payloads lik_specs/ (B1+B2 migration); rebuild v13 headers, logic changes needed. * tulpaObs never used legacy ratio path; rebuild v13. * tulpaGlmm Day-22+ already targets generic path; rebuild v13.

what: tulpa 2026-05-11 — NNGP Laplace: full off-diagonal precision scatter
title: tulpa 2026-05-11 — NNGP Laplace: full off-diagonal precision scatter
text: laplace_mode_gp (spatial-/ ST-combo NNGP entries nested_laplace.cpp) now assemble full NNGP precision matrix Λ = (- )' D⁻¹ (- ) every Newton iteration, replacing diagonal--w approximation kept 1/v_i focal diagonal row. missed : gradient contribution neighbours (+a_{,k}·q_i/v_i), -diagonal Hessian entries (focal, neighbour_k) (neighbour_k, neighbour_kp), pairwise precision members every conditioning set. Newton mode w therefore shrunk toward zero pointwise field recovery smooth latent fields collapsed (cor ≈ 0). batch_nngp_scatter(..., alpha_out = nullptr) — backward-compatible extra optional output capturing per-row conditional regression weights (already computed internally; just exposed). apply_nngp_full_prior_dense — scatters full precision contribution dense (grad, H) pair via alpha + cv bundle. apply_nngp_full_prior_sparse — , SparseHessianBuilder. make_nngp_prior_sparsity_pattern — emits (row, col) pairs required back sparse path. Wired four scatter call sites: laplace_mode_gp dense Newton, laplace_mode_gp sparse Newton (pattern expansion), spatial-cpp_nested_laplace_nngp scatter lambda, make_nngp_spatial_ops::add_prior_at_k (ST-combo NNGP block). Log-prior calls (log_prior lambdas) unchanged — need cm cv, existing batch_nngp_scatter signature still supports without alpha_out. Effect (downstream measurement tulpaGlmm Day-31 smoke): cor(w_mean, f_true) jumps near zero ≈ 0.81 Pearson 120-location Poisson + smooth-GP simulation. β recovery unchanged. Additive: TULPA_ABI_VERSION bump (still v10). Public shim signatures unchanged; inner Laplace scatter upgraded. Downstream packages must rebuild commit pick new behaviour (source changes required).
